Bún Chả 145
Jan 2025 • Solo
Buncha 145 in Vietnam offers a delicious and authentic experience for those craving traditional Vietnamese dishes. The signature bun cha, with its tender grilled pork, flavorful broth, and fresh herbs, is a standout. The atmosphere is casual and welcoming, perfect for a quick and satisfying meal. The service is friendly and efficient, making it a great spot for anyone looking to enjoy a tasty, no-frills Vietnamese meal. Highly recommended for both locals and tourists!

After seeing it being top listed as 'must try' place in various articles, I added it to the list of places to try when in HCMC.

Day 1: reached place at 7:45 pm to find a queue and decided to join it. But the owner (a very nice person) shared that they close at 8 pm and requested me not to wait. 

Day 2 : reached the place at 7 pm, to again find a queue... 11 people in front of me. Undettered, I decided to wait it out.

Started noting about the interiors. It was a narrow but longer in shape. There were 11 twin seaters tables along either sides with a central alley. These tables are joined to accommodate bigger groups. The seats towards the walls were CI twin benches. The other seat was a smaller single seater seat.
Decor was minimalistic or non existent. 

The line moved faster than expected and in about 15 minutes, I got seated. Fortunately, they were not asking strangers to share tables to maximise business. So I appreciated the privacy even when there was a long queue behind me.

The menu was limited; but it was very helpful with pictures and description in English.
Along with the menu, they handed a order sheet, where I was to tick out my order. Had some query, which was quickly clarified by the very friendly owner / manager.

So I ordered the bun Cha (what else), one fried beef wrapped in leave and an ice tea.

Service was quite prompt. The fried beef was served as a starter which was quickly followed by the bun Cha. 

The fried beef wrapped in leaf was served on a stick, on a plate with sauce and a thin sliced of red chilli. Presentation / plating was impressive. Portion size .... hmmm let me say 'french influence'.

The bun Cha was no different. 4 pcs of meat (2 minced mini patty and 2 pcs of slice) were in the soup. The noodle portion was small.... was finished in 6 feeding portions. Veggies were just adequate for the served portions.

Taste : the fried wrapped beef was an experience but the bun Cha was nothing special. Infact, I would not even put in top 5 of places where I tried bun Cha.

Since I was planning this to be my dinner, and the French sized portions is not exactly how I like my meals; I had to quickly summon the owner and requested him to add a dessert... the fried banana. And did I do good.... 
It's presentation was impressive, portion size (nothing new to add) and taste... excellent. It was covered with crispy rice and had a chocolate sauce on a small dish. It was an experience worth having.

The whole meal was just 103k vnd (under $5). So was a very good value for money. 

So while I would not go bashing them for small portion sizes and over hyped expectations created by the buzz, I would credit them for offering an opportunity to actually try their entire menu. It will definitely serve two person a balanced portion or for a single person just short of overload.

I would recommend a visit to this place without too much expectation, and a mindset to sample different varieties instead one dish meal.

Bui Vien is a very VERY busy tourist street because it is in the central back packers area of district 1 and just CRAWLING with white international travelers with targets on their backs (and their wallets!). Yuk....

Because of this there are just hundreds of pushy street sellers trying to hock their rubbish to the thousands of targets that roam the bars.

And man is it busy! Bars and restaurants that cater to Western tourists. You can find Western beers, burgers and pizza... everything we WEREN'T looking for, but nestled between some of the crappy over priced tourist bars lies Bun Cha. 

What a find - thank you Trip Advisor reviewers!

As we were looking to eat early at around 5.30pm our options were still plentiful, but our mission was to find and eat at Bun Cha.

They open for dinner right on 5.30pm and we already had to wait in line behind locals to get in. A very good sign!

5.30pm rolled up and the doors opened. Already the smells were enough to make my mouth water, and start my belly rumbling!

Upon sitting down we were given a picture menu and an ordering form to fill in.

Most of the wait staff are deaf, so hence the order forms, but this is clearly noted on a sign at the front door. Don't for a minute think this will hinder your experience... not at all.

We chose 3 mains, a fish ball dish, a beef and noodle dish (number 1 on the menu), and the black spring rolls (I believe this is a Hanoi dish), and I can honestly say all of them were delicious! So much so we had to stop ourselves from ordering EVERYTHING else on the menu and filling ourselves to the brim!

The service is very fast and very efficient, probably because they only have about 7-8 tables and customer turnover is very swift. Average time for dinner would be 15-25 minutes, as the service is soooo fast! I don't mean that they hurry you out, because they don't. I mean that after 25 minutes, you have enjoyed multiple dishes that appear quickly right off the stove, and you are ready to move on. 

We paid d108,000 for 3 mains, an iced tea and a bottle of water, which equated to about USD$. 

FANTASTIC value when you consider the tourist bars will sell you one small pizza for $10USD and gin and tonics with hardly any gin in them for $7USD

All in all a great experience, and one I wish we could repeat if time allowed.

Highly recommended, and if you can only order one or two dishes, the fish balls wrapped in rice is a MUST, as is the beef and noodle dish (number 1).

Small Restaurant. Inexpensive. Delicious. Bún Chả - A Hanoi Specialty in Saigon
Apr 2017 • Solo
This is a small restaurant and on some nights, there will be line waiting to get a table. Their specialty (and restaurant name) is Bún Chả. This is a combination of broth, BBQ pork, fresh vegetables, and noodles. Order the Nem (fried spring rolls) too, as that is part of the meal and an inexpensive addition on the menu.

There are a few Bún Chả restaurants in Saigon (Ho Chi Minh City), but I like this one. Partly, this is because it is on the colorful and always busy Bùi Viện Street, in the heart of the Backpacker District. Look at your food, or gaze outside at the humanity strolling past. You won't be bored.

Try this restaurant if you are in the area. You will have tried something that is harder to find in this section of Saigon, but that is an authentic Vietnamese specialty food. Everything is clean and fresh, so you should not be concerned about the healthiness of the food.

Bun Cha was the first proper Vietnamese dish I ate, when we landed in Hanoi, three weeks prior to visiting this little gem in Ho Chi Minh City. It basically is a broth (made with garlic, fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, pickled papaya,;..) in which caramelized charcoal grilled pieces of ground pork float and swim. You add greens and noodles, after seasoning with chile and garlic and off you go. The original dish comes from Hanoi but we were delighted to find this place here, as we were heading out of the country from the south. 

While there was a bit of a cue going on (we went there at about 20h in the evening), the people from the restaurant took out little chairs for us to wait on the sidewalk and provided us with menus and ordering pamphlets. 

When we finally sat down inside the small but nice and clean restaurant, we only had to wait 10 mins for our orders: 2 times the classic bun cha, and beef skewers and spring rolls for the kids (they had enough of bun cha and street food at this point in our trip). 

Quality of the food was great, it even surpassed the first one I had in Hanoi, beating the original. So we ordered 2 more just to delight in this a bit further before heading home. 

Prices are very reasonable, verging to the cheap, so if you are ever in Ho Chi Minh you can not afford missing out on this. 

As desserts we had the famous deep fried fruit spring rolls (cold in the middle, hot on the outside) but as we aren't really dessert people and we've already had too much of the main course that was a bit lost. I could see why people like it though, it is a great combination and people around us were raving about the quality.

Nestled between the throng of ex-pat bars and overpriced restaurants offering inauthentic noodles to backpackers looking for a cheap drink, is this complete star of a place. Grrrr! How can I tell you to keep it to yourself while still wanting to share this place with others to encourage the trade that they truly deserve?! While by no means the most experienced travellers in HCMC we have at least spent the last couple of months seeing what not only this city but also many other places in Vietnam have to offer culinarily and have to say that this really ranks amongst the top in all of the categories that really count for the food loving visitor on a budget, namely; taste, price and service! For 35'000vnd you will be treated to a great example of Bun Cha served in a beautifully decorated restaurant by friendly and welcoming staff. 
For those of you not familiar with Bun Cha, a dish usually famous throughout Hanoi, it is a selection of grilled pork slices and tasty meatballs in a hot (although sometimes cold - not my preference) thin broth, garnished with vegetables and served with a fresh green leafy salad and cooked, cold noodles. Alongside this are fresh chilies and pickled garlic to taste. Dipping your noodles a bite at a time into the broth warms them through and all in all makes for a very tasty and very filling dish. 
And at Bun Cha 145 it is amongst the best that we have tried. 
Their menu is not huge but doesn't have to be, as we have slowly worked our way through nearly all of the lovely accompaniments that you can order, from grilled beef stuffed into green pepper leaves, to hot fried pork balls and more! To be honest all are beautifully presented and served and I really do have trouble picking a favourite! Try them all, seriously! At between 12k to 35k for most of them you really wont break the bank and the drinks, beer and fruit juices are also all incredibly reasonable at 10k to 25k so there is no excuse to not really set about the whole menu. It stuns me that given some of the shoddy bars and restaurants that are in this locale selling the same old dishes at triple the honest price, that Bun Cha 145 isn't packed out, with queues around the block. And there is my conundrum! Really do give them your trade but, please, please save a table for us! 
Did I mention that there is only one other review! Inconceivable!
